market_view: Calm but rate-pressured regime: VIX 15.2 (+6.6% on the day, -18.6% over 20 days) while the 30-year yield hit a 19-year high above 5.33% (CNBC) and the 10y is at 4.72%, near its 52-week high. The main new fact is the expiry of the US-Iran ceasefire, which reopens the oil supply-shock storyline.

oil_gas.catalyst: 'Oil prices jump after US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens Oman' (The Guardian, 2026-08-18). A ceasefire that has expired, plus a threat toward Oman (a state on the Strait of Hormuz), is a named escalation. Crude is still 14% below its level of 60 days ago and only +1.5% over 20 days, so a renewed war risk premium is not fully rebuilt yet.
oil_gas.reasoning: This is a regime-level escalation, not a one-off incident, and it comes after a 60-day crude decline rather than a long run. WTI was already up 2.55% on Aug 17, so part of the move is priced; the confidence stays modest. Downside risk: a quick new truce or Trump pressure on oil-company profits.

gold_miners.reasoning: NEM is up 35% in 20 days, and the only headlines are a Cadia community grant and an FT letter about central-bank repatriation. Rising long yields work against gold. There is no named catalyst.

chips.reasoning: Nvidia's $105B OpenAI data-center financing (CNBC) adds balance-sheet risk as much as demand. The 'SOX plunges over 6%' headline (BigGo) conflicts with the record's +1.06% SOX day, so it is unreliable. Late-August earnings add variance only.

pharma.catalyst: none new; the Q2 guidance raise is now about two weeks old
pharma.reasoning: The existing LLY hold (renewed 08-13) runs to about 08-27. I am not renewing it: LLY fell 4% in 5 days with no headline to explain it, the record has no LLY news, and the guidance-raise drift is stale. The only pharma headline is irrelevant.

copper_uranium.catalyst: The Congo concentrate export ban is still in force (carried storyline, no reversal or exemption in the record); also 'Walz executive order moves to block copper mining near the Boundary Waters' (MPR News, 2026-08-18), which adds a small US supply restriction. Copper is 1.5% off its 52-week high, and supply bans tend to persist for weeks.
copper_uranium.reasoning: The supply story is intact and FCX recovered 2.8% on Aug 17 after a 5-day dip. Risks: an exemption to the Congo ban, demand or tariff shocks, and high long yields. Confidence is at the bar.

would_change_my_mind: A new US-Iran truce or Hormuz reopening deal (oil), an exemption to or reversal of the Congo export ban (copper), or a company-specific NVDA or LLY headline.

handoff.what_changed: The US-Iran ceasefire expired and Trump threatened Oman (Guardian); crude rose 2.6% on Aug 17, so I re-entered XOM. The 30-year yield hit a 19-year high above 5.33% (CNBC). Walz moved to block copper mining near the Boundary Waters (MPR News); there is no Congo ban reversal.
